_about: Cost-allocation model of Incoterms 2020 used by glops.landed. S = seller pays, B = buyer pays. This is a MODEL of the rules for cost estimation, not the ICC text. The binding text is the ICC publication 'Incoterms 2020' (ICC Pub. No. 723E), which is not freely available; the split below was checked against the public sources listed in 'sources' and the notes record every point where those sources say the answer depends on the contract.

sources.icc: ICC, 'Incoterms 2020' rules page, https://iccwbo.org/business-solutions/incoterms-rules/incoterms-2020/ (accessed 2026-10-13): CIF default cover Institute Cargo Clauses (C); CIP requires Institute Cargo Clauses (A); DPU replaces DAT and the seller unloads; under DAP the seller does not unload; costs consolidated in A9/B9.
sources.trade_gov: U.S. International Trade Administration, 'Know Your Incoterms', https://www.trade.gov/know-your-incoterms (accessed 2026-10-13): 11 rules, 7 any-mode and 4 sea/inland-waterway only; each rule allocates export/import clearance, carriage, insurance.
sources.wikipedia: Wikipedia, 'Incoterms' (Incoterms 2020 cost-allocation table), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incoterms (accessed 2026-10-13). Secondary summary; used for the row-by-row table.
sources.gw: Gebrueder Weiss, 'Incoterms 2020', https://www.gw-world.com/incoterms (accessed 2026-10-13). Secondary summary by a freight forwarder; used to cross-check FCA variants, DAP/DPU unloading, C-rule unloading at destination ('if specified in the contract of carriage').
sources.tfg_cif: Trade Finance Global, 'Cost Insurance Freight (CIF)' guide, https://www.tradefinanceglobal.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Cost__Insurance__Freight_CIF.pdf (accessed 2026-10-13): insurance at least 110% of the contract price.

elements.label: Export packaging
elements.note: A8 in every rule: seller packages at its own cost unless agreed otherwise. Treated as part of the seller's base (EXW) price.

elements.label: Loading at seller's premises
elements.note: EXW: buyer (seller has no loading obligation). FCA at seller's premises: seller loads onto buyer's vehicle (A2).

elements.label: Export customs clearance
elements.note: EXW: buyer. All other rules: seller (A7).

elements.label: Pre-carriage to export terminal
elements.note: FCA: depends on the named place. At seller's premises -> buyer; at a terminal -> seller (seller delivers on its own vehicle ready for unloading). Wikipedia shows 'Buyer/Seller'.

elements.label: Unloading / receiving at export terminal
elements.note: FCA: buyer (seller's delivery ends 'ready for unloading'). FAS/FOB/C/D: seller.

elements.label: Loading on vessel / aircraft (origin THC)
elements.note: FAS: buyer (delivery is alongside). FOB, C and D rules: seller. In practice origin THC under FOB is a frequent dispute; the model follows the rule (seller pays until on board).

elements.label: Main carriage (international freight)
elements.note: Seller contracts carriage under C and D rules; buyer under E and F rules.

elements.label: Cargo insurance (main leg)
elements.note: Only CIF (min. ICC (C)) and CIP (ICC (A)) oblige the seller to insure, at least 110% of the contract price. For all other rules there is NO insurance obligation; the model charges insurance to the party bearing transit risk (column 'risk'), which is a modelling assumption, not an Incoterms obligation.

elements.label: Unloading at import terminal (destination THC)
elements.note: UNCERTAIN BY DESIGN for C rules: buyer pays unless the seller's contract of carriage includes it (A9/B9; gw: 'if specified in the contract of carriage'). Model default: buyer; switch 'c_rules_carriage_includes_dest_thc' to move it to the seller. D rules: seller (part of carriage to the named place).

elements.label: Import customs clearance (broker, permits)
elements.note: Buyer in every rule except DDP.

elements.label: Import duty
elements.note: Buyer in every rule except DDP.

elements.label: Import VAT / GST
elements.note: Buyer in every rule except DDP. Whether it is a real cost depends on whether the importer of record can recover it as input tax (model flags).

elements.label: On-carriage to final destination
elements.note: D rules: seller. C rules: buyer when the named place is the port/airport of destination (model default); for CPT/CIP the parties may name the buyer's premises, which moves on-carriage to the seller ('cpt_cip_named_place_is_buyer_premises').

elements.label: Unloading at final destination
elements.note: Only DPU makes the seller unload. DAP and DDP: goods delivered 'ready for unloading' -> buyer.

EXW.delivery: Goods placed at the disposal of the buyer at the named place (seller's premises), not loaded.

FCA.delivery: Named place = seller's premises: when loaded on the buyer's means of transport. (Variant FCA_TERMINAL: when on seller's vehicle at the named terminal, ready for unloading.)

FCA_TERMINAL.delivery: FCA with the named place at the export terminal: goods on the seller's vehicle, ready for unloading.

FAS.delivery: Alongside the vessel nominated by the buyer at the named port of shipment.

FOB.delivery: On board the vessel nominated by the buyer at the named port of shipment.

CFR.delivery: On board the vessel at the port of shipment; seller pays freight to the named port of destination.

CIF.delivery: As CFR; seller also insures (min. ICC (C), 110% of contract price).

CPT.delivery: Handed to the first carrier contracted by the seller; seller pays carriage to the named place of destination.

CIP.delivery: As CPT; seller also insures (ICC (A), 110% of contract price).

DAP.delivery: At the named place of destination, on the arriving means of transport, ready for unloading.

DPU.delivery: Unloaded at the named place of destination.

DDP.delivery: At the named place of destination, cleared for import, ready for unloading.
